subject: Deployment blackout and SLA exceptions — action items
messages:
From: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@helioscloud.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helioscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA v3 + support requirements (Helios migration)

Avery —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Attached is our consolidated redline to the MSA (redline_MSA_v3.pdf) and a short support matrix that shows the SLAs we require for the migration period. High-level asks from Helios: 

- Uptime: 99.99% for the production tenant during the first 90 days post-cutover.
- P1 response time: initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes and remediation SLA of 4 hours.
- Maintenance: we need a hard blackout for any scheduled platform deployment that could impact latency or availability during our migration windows (target windows: weekends 02:00-10:00 PT on the weeks of Feb 20 and Mar 5).
- Service credits: automatic, prorated credits if uptime falls below the committed threshold; also a cap that covers Helios’s migration risk.

We know some of these are out of your standard support tiers, but given the scale and timing of this migration we wanted to put everything on the table so Redwood can flag exceptions/constraints up front. If you can get ops/legal eyes on the redline and send a list of the items you can accept versus those requiring escalation, that would help us prioritize.

Tim
Tim Baxter
Head of Cloud Platform — Helios Cloud
tim.baxter@helioscloud.com

Attachments: redline_MSA_v3.pdf, support_matrix.xlsx

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@helioscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA v3 + support requirements (Helios migration)

All — looping you in. Helios sent their redline and a support matrix; they want 99.99% and a 30-minute P1 ack for the first 90 days, plus a hard deployment blackout during two weekend migration windows.

Marissa — can you lead commercial response on credits and escalation path? We should propose a short-term migration addendum instead of permanently changing the global SLA.

Connor — ops: please review the maintenance blackout ask and confirm whether we can guarantee no platform deployments during those two weekends, or if we need a carveout (e.g., emergency fixes only with advance notice). If ops cannot guarantee a zero-deploy window, outline the mitigations and rollback guarantees we can offer.

Laura — legal, I’ve attached Tim’s file; would appreciate a very targeted pass on the proposed uptime/credit language and any recommended alternative phrasing (e.g., an explicit migration addendum, conditional credits, or timeboxed elevated SLA).

Goal: get a firm counter to Helios by EOD Wednesday so procurement can move to DocuSign next week if we align.

Thanks —
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@helioscloud.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA v3 + support requirements (Helios migration)

Tim — thanks for sending the redline and the matrix. We reviewed with ops and legal; below is our proposed path forward to keep migration risk low while protecting our standard terms: 

1) Migration Addendum (preferred): short, timeboxed addendum that elevates certain SLAs for a 90-day migration window only. Key points:
   - Commitment: 99.95% uptime for the migration window (operationally achievable with reserved capacity and dedicated on-call).
   - P1 response: 30-minute acknowledgement, target remediation within 6 hours (we can commit to 4 hours when on dedicated response coverage as a paid add-on).
   - Credits: automatic prorated credits for downtime below the 99.95% threshold, with a one-time additional migration credit pool (capped at 5% of monthly fees during the migration window) to address Helios migration exposure.

2) Maintenance / deployment blackout: Connor confirms we can avoid planned platform releases in Helios’s migration weekends, but cannot absolutely prevent emergency patches. Ops proposes a protocol:
   - No scheduled deployments during the requested windows (02:00–10:00 PT).
   - Emergency releases allowed only with 4-hour advance notice to Helios (where feasible) and with our rollback plan documented.
   - For additional risk reduction, we can allocate a warmed, dedicated pool for Helios traffic for the first 30 days (costable).

3) Legal redlines: Laura, below are specific asks from Helios we cannot accept as-is (e.g., permanent 99.99% uplift and unconditional 30-min remediation). We suggest the migration addendum approach and will attach suggested language.

Would you be open to the migration addendum route? If so we’ll draft a 1–2 page addendum and a short SOW for the dedicated coverage option. If Helios insists on 99.99% and unconditional 30-min remediation without the addendum premium or dedicated pool, we’ll need exec approval and a different pricing structure.

I’ve attached a draft support_matrix.xlsx that maps the proposed migration credit pool and the dedicated pool pricing.

Let us know and we’ll get the addendum over for a quick review.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: support_matrix.xlsx

From: Tim Baxter <tim.baxter@helioscloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement <procurement@helioscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Jan 2028 13:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: MSA v3 + support requirements (Helios migration)

Marissa — this looks reasonable and thanks for the clear options. We prefer the Migration Addendum approach (timeboxed uplift + limited credit pool) to avoid permanently changing the MSA. Two quick asks to unblock procurement: 

- Please put the migration addendum in simple redline form (1–2 pages) and indicate the cost for the dedicated warmed pool for 30 days.
- Can you confirm the emergency patch protocol and the 4-hr notice expectation in the addendum? Helios procurement needs wording that prevents surprise disruptive pushes during the cutover.

If you can send the addendum draft by Wednesday EOD we’ll route it through Procurement and Legal and aim to DocuSign next week. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Tim
Tim Baxter
Head of Cloud Platform — Helios Cloud
tim.baxter@helioscloud.com
